objects.description: No custom data types (structs, enums, typedefs, or classes) are defined in this header. The file only defines a large set of numeric macros mapping binary-like identifiers (e.g., B1011) to their decimal values. There are no user-defined types to extract.

Built-in C type; not a custom type defined by this header. No custom structs, enums, typedefs, or classes are defined in this file. The header only declares the C function dtostrf for formatting a double into a string.
Alias of void used to mimic AVR pgmspace types on non-AVR platforms. Behaves exactly like void for type purposes.
Alias of char representing a character stored in program memory on AVR. Here it is equivalent to char.
Alias of unsigned char for AVR program-memory compatibility. Equivalent to unsigned char.
Alias of int8_t for AVR program-memory compatibility. Equivalent to int8_t.
Alias of uint8_t for AVR program-memory compatibility. Equivalent to uint8_t.
Alias of int16_t for AVR program-memory compatibility. Equivalent to int16_t.
Alias of uint16_t for AVR program-memory compatibility. Equivalent to uint16_t.
Alias of int32_t for AVR program-memory compatibility. Equivalent to int32_t.
Alias of uint32_t for AVR program-memory compatibility. Equivalent to uint32_t.
Alias of int64_t for AVR program-memory compatibility. Equivalent to int64_t.
Alias of uint64_t for AVR program-memory compatibility. Equivalent to uint64_t.

functions.name: itoa
functions.description: Converts the integer value to a null-terminated character string representation in the specified numeric base (radix) and writes it into the provided buffer, returning the buffer pointer. Typical usage: provide a writable buffer and a base (e.g., 10 for decimal, 16 for hex). This is a non-standard but common utility provided by Arduino headers; exact formatting details (e.g., handling of negative values for non-decimal bases) are implementation-defined and not specified in this header.
requirements: string must be a non-null pointer to a writable buffer.
The buffer pointed to by string must be large enough to hold the converted number including the terminating '\0' (exact required size depends on value and radix; not specified here).
radix must be a supported base for conversion; commonly 2–36 in similar implementations, but the accepted range for this header is not specified.
Behavior for negative values with non-decimal radices is implementation-defined/unspecified in this header.
Return value is documented only by convention: typically returns string; whether it can return NULL on error is unspecified.

functions.name: ltoa
functions.description: Converts the long integer value to a null-terminated character string in the specified base (radix), storing the result into the provided buffer and returning the buffer pointer. Usage mirrors itoa but for long values. Exact formatting details are implementation-defined and not specified here.
requirements: string must be a non-null pointer to a writable buffer.
The buffer must be large enough for the converted representation, including the terminating '\0' (exact size not specified).
radix must be a supported base; commonly 2–36 in similar implementations, but the accepted range is not specified here.
Behavior for negative values with non-decimal radices is implementation-defined/unspecified in this header.
Return value is by convention the input buffer pointer; whether NULL can be returned on error is unspecified.

functions.name: utoa
functions.description: Converts an unsigned integer value to its null-terminated character string representation in the given base (radix), writing into the provided buffer and returning the buffer pointer. Note: This signature is conditionally compiled for certain GCC versions; see header guards. Formatting specifics are not documented here.
requirements: string must be a non-null pointer to a writable buffer.
The buffer must be large enough to hold the converted number plus the terminating '\0' (exact size not specified).
radix must be a supported base; commonly 2–36 in similar implementations, but the accepted range is not specified here.
Return value is typically string; whether NULL can be returned on error is unspecified.
This signature is available only when the compiler condition in the header selects it (GCC > 4.9.2); otherwise see the unsigned long variant below.

functions.name: ultoa
functions.signature: char *ultoa(unsigned long value, char *string, int radix)
functions.description: Converts an unsigned long value to a null-terminated character string in the specified base (radix), storing the result into the provided buffer and returning the buffer pointer. Intended for unsigned long conversions. Exact formatting details are not specified in this header.
requirements: string must be a non-null pointer to a writable buffer.
The buffer must be large enough to hold the converted number including the terminating '\0' (exact size not specified).
radix must be a supported base; commonly 2–36 in similar implementations, but the accepted range is not specified here.
Return value is typically string; whether NULL can be returned on error is unspecified.

functions.name: dtostrf
functions.signature: char *dtostrf(double val, signed char width, unsigned char prec, char *sout);
functions.description: Converts the floating-point value val to a C string with the specified formatting and writes the result into the buffer pointed to by sout. The result uses a minimum field width given by width and prints prec digits after the decimal point, emulating avr-libc’s dtostrf behavior. Returns sout. Typical usage is to format a double for display or serial output without using printf on embedded platforms. Notes: In avr-libc semantics, a negative width indicates left-justification; non-negative width right-justifies within the field. Details not present in this header are inferred from the standard dtostrf behavior.
requirements: sout must be a valid, writable pointer to a character buffer.
The buffer at sout must be large enough to hold the formatted number plus the terminating null character.
width specifies the minimum field width; if negative, the output is left-justified (inferred from avr-libc dtostrf semantics).
prec specifies the number of digits after the decimal point; it is treated as an unsigned quantity.
The function returns sout; callers should not assume any error indicator beyond the contents of the output string.

functions.name: memchr_P
functions.signature: void *memchr_P(const void *s, int c, size_t n)
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to memchr. Searches the first n bytes of the memory block pointed to by s for the byte value c and returns a pointer to the first match, or NULL if not found. Intended to mirror AVR PROGMEM APIs on non-AVR targets.
requirements: s must be a valid pointer to a readable memory region of at least n bytes.
n may be zero; if zero, the function returns NULL without accessing memory.
c is interpreted as an unsigned char value in the search.
Returned pointer, if non-NULL, points within the range [s, (char*)s + n).

functions.name: memcmp_P
functions.signature: int memcmp_P(const void *s1, const void *s2, size_t n)
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to memcmp. Compares the first n bytes of two memory blocks s1 and s2. Returns <0, 0, or >0 if s1 is lexicographically less than, equal to, or greater than s2. Mirrors AVR PROGMEM API.
requirements: s1 and s2 must point to readable memory regions of at least n bytes each.
n may be zero; no memory is accessed if n is zero.

functions.name: memcpy_P
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to memcpy. Copies n bytes from src to dest. Behavior is undefined if regions overlap. Mirrors AVR PROGMEM sources on non-AVR.
requirements: dest must point to a writable memory region of at least n bytes.
src must point to a readable memory region of at least n bytes.
Memory regions must not overlap; use memmove for overlapping ranges.
Returns dest.

functions.name: memmem_P
functions.signature: void *memmem_P(const void *haystack, size_t haystacklen, const void *needle, size_t needlelen)
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to GNU memmem. Searches the memory region haystack (length haystacklen) for the first occurrence of the byte sequence needle (length needlelen). Returns a pointer to the first occurrence or NULL if not found.
requirements: haystack must point to a readable memory region of at least haystacklen bytes.
If needlelen is 0, the result is implementation-defined for memmem; commonly returns (void*)haystack.
If haystacklen is 0 and needlelen > 0, returns NULL.
Return pointer, if any, points within haystack.

functions.name: memrchr_P
functions.signature: void *memrchr_P(const void *s, int c, size_t n)
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to GNU memrchr. Searches the last n bytes of the memory block s for the last occurrence of byte value c and returns a pointer to the match, or NULL if not found.
requirements: s must be a valid pointer to a readable memory region of at least n bytes.
c is matched as an unsigned char value.
If n is 0, returns NULL without accessing memory.

functions.name: strcat_P
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to strcat. Appends the C-string src to the end of dest and returns dest. Mirrors AVR PROGMEM API for program-space strings.
requirements: dest must be a writable, NUL-terminated string with enough space to hold its original content plus strlen(src)+1 bytes.
src must be a valid NUL-terminated string.
Behavior is undefined if the buffers overlap or if dest lacks sufficient space.

functions.name: strchr_P
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to strchr. Locates the first occurrence of character c (interpreted as unsigned char) in string s, including the terminating NUL. Returns pointer to the character or NULL if not found.
requirements: s must be a valid NUL-terminated string.
c may be '\0' to find the terminator.

functions.name: strchrnul_P
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to GNU strchrnul. Returns a pointer to the first occurrence of c in s, or to the terminating NUL if c is not found.
requirements: s must be a valid NUL-terminated string.
c is interpreted as unsigned char for matching.

functions.name: strcmp_P
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to strcmp. Lexicographically compares two NUL-terminated strings and returns <0, 0, or >0 based on ordering.
requirements: s1 and s2 must be valid NUL-terminated strings.

functions.name: strcpy_P
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to strcpy. Copies the NUL-terminated string src to dest, including the terminator, and returns dest.
requirements: dest must be writable with capacity >= strlen(src)+1.
src must be a valid NUL-terminated string.
Behavior is undefined if buffers overlap.

functions.name: strcasecmp_P
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to strcasecmp (case-insensitive compare). Returns <0, 0, or >0 ignoring case differences.
requirements: s1 and s2 must be valid NUL-terminated strings.
Case mapping follows the current locale if the C library uses locale-aware behavior.

functions.name: strcasestr_P
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to strcasestr (case-insensitive substring search). Returns a pointer to the first occurrence of needle in haystack, ignoring case, or NULL if not found.
requirements: haystack and needle must be valid NUL-terminated strings.
If needle is empty, returns haystack.

functions.name: strlcat_P
functions.signature: size_t strlcat_P(char *dest, const char *src, size_t size)
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to BSD strlcat. Appends src to dest of total size size, ensuring NUL-termination if size > 0. Returns the length it tried to create (initial length of dest plus length of src).
requirements: dest must be a NUL-terminated string unless size is 0.
dest must have a writable buffer of at least size bytes.
src must be a valid NUL-terminated string.
Caller should check return value >= size to detect truncation.

functions.name: strlcpy_P
functions.signature: size_t strlcpy_P(char *dest, const char *src, size_t size)
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to BSD strlcpy. Copies src to dest of size size, NUL-terminating if size > 0. Returns the length of src.
requirements: dest must be a writable buffer of at least size bytes (can be zero).
src must be a valid NUL-terminated string.
Caller should check return value >= size to detect truncation.

functions.name: strlen_P
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to strlen. Returns the length of the NUL-terminated string s (number of characters before the terminator).
requirements: s must be a valid NUL-terminated string.

functions.name: strnlen_P
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to strnlen. Returns the length of s limited to at most maxlen; does not read past maxlen bytes.
requirements: s must point to a readable memory region of at least maxlen bytes or to a NUL-terminated string shorter than maxlen.

functions.name: strncmp_P
functions.signature: int strncmp_P(const char *s1, const char *s2, size_t n)
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to strncmp. Compares up to n characters of two strings and returns <0, 0, or >0.
requirements: s1 and s2 must be readable strings; they need not be NUL-terminated if a difference is found before n characters.
n may be zero; then result is 0 and no memory is accessed.

functions.name: strncasecmp_P
functions.signature: int strncasecmp_P(const char *s1, const char *s2, size_t n)
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to strncasecmp (case-insensitive). Compares up to n characters ignoring case; returns <0, 0, or >0.
requirements: s1 and s2 must be readable strings.
n may be zero; then result is 0 and no memory is accessed.

functions.name: strncat_P
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to strncat. Appends at most n characters from src to dest and NUL-terminates the result. Returns dest.
requirements: dest must be a writable, NUL-terminated string with enough space for min(n, strlen(src)) + 1 additional bytes.
src must be a valid NUL-terminated string.
Undefined behavior if buffers overlap.

functions.name: strncpy_P
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to strncpy. Copies at most n characters from src to dest. If src is shorter than n, dest is padded with NUL bytes; otherwise dest is not NUL-terminated. Returns dest.
requirements: dest must be a writable buffer of at least n bytes.
src must be a readable string.
Caller must ensure NUL-termination if src length >= n and NUL-termination is required.

functions.name: strpbrk_P
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to strpbrk. Returns a pointer to the first character in s that matches any character in accept, or NULL if none.
requirements: s and accept must be valid NUL-terminated strings.

functions.name: strrchr_P
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to strrchr. Returns a pointer to the last occurrence of character c in s, including the terminating NUL if c is '\0', or NULL if not found.
requirements: s must be a valid NUL-terminated string.
c is interpreted as unsigned char for matching.

functions.name: strsep_P
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to BSD strsep. Parses tokens in-place in *stringp by replacing the next delimiter with NUL; returns the token start and advances *stringp, or returns NULL if *stringp is NULL.
requirements: stringp must be a non-NULL pointer to a modifiable char* (or may be NULL to return NULL).
*stringp must either be NULL or point to a writable, NUL-terminated string (the function writes NUL terminators).
delim must be a valid NUL-terminated string of delimiter characters.

functions.name: strspn_P
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to strspn. Returns the length of the initial segment of s consisting entirely of characters from accept.
requirements: s and accept must be valid NUL-terminated strings.

functions.name: strstr_P
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to strstr. Returns a pointer to the first occurrence of needle in haystack, or NULL if not found.
requirements: haystack and needle must be valid NUL-terminated strings.
If needle is empty, returns haystack.

functions.name: sprintf_P
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to sprintf. Formats data according to format into the buffer str and returns the number of characters written (excluding the NUL terminator).
requirements: str must point to a writable buffer large enough to hold the formatted result including the terminating NUL; sprintf does not perform bounds checking.
format must be a valid printf-style format string matching the provided arguments.
Using sprintf with insufficient buffer space causes buffer overflow and undefined behavior. Prefer snprintf_P when possible.

functions.name: vfprintf_P
functions.signature: int vfprintf_P(FILE *stream, const char *format, va_list ap)
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to vfprintf. Writes formatted output to stream using the argument list ap. Returns number of characters written or a negative value on error.
requirements: stream must be a valid FILE* opened for writing.
format must be a valid printf-style format string corresponding to the arguments in ap.
ap must be a properly initialized va_list and should not be used again after a corresponding va_end in the caller's scope without reinitialization.

functions.name: printf_P
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to printf. Writes formatted output to stdout. Returns number of characters written or negative on error.
requirements: format must be a valid printf-style format string and must match the provided arguments.

functions.name: snprintf_P
functions.signature: int snprintf_P(char *str, size_t size, const char *format, ...)
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to snprintf. Formats data into str, writing at most size bytes including the terminating NUL. Returns the number of characters that would have been written (excluding the NUL) or a negative value on error.
requirements: str must point to a writable buffer of at least size bytes (can be zero).
format must be a valid printf-style format string matching the provided arguments.
Caller should check the return value >= size to detect truncation.

functions.name: vsprintf_P
functions.signature: int vsprintf_P(char *str, const char *format, va_list ap)
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to vsprintf. Formats data into str using argument list ap. Returns the number of characters written (excluding NUL).
requirements: str must point to a writable buffer large enough for the formatted output; vsprintf does not do bounds checking.
format must be a valid printf-style format string for the arguments in ap.
ap must be a properly initialized va_list.

functions.name: vsnprintf_P
functions.signature: int vsnprintf_P(char *str, size_t size, const char *format, va_list ap)
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to vsnprintf. Formats output into str using ap, writing at most size bytes including the NUL terminator. Returns the number of characters that would have been written (excluding NUL) or a negative value on error.
requirements: str must be a writable buffer of at least size bytes (can be zero).
format must be a valid printf-style format string for the arguments in ap.
ap must be a properly initialized va_list.
Caller should check return value >= size to detect truncation.

functions.name: fprintf_P
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to fprintf. Writes formatted output to the given stream. Returns number of characters written or negative on error.
requirements: stream must be a valid FILE* opened for writing.
format must be a valid printf-style format string matching the provided arguments.

functions.name: strlen_PF
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to strlen. PF variant (functionally identical here) for program-memory FAR pointers on AVR; on this platform it is an alias. Returns length of s.
requirements: s must be a valid NUL-terminated string.

functions.name: strnlen_PF
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to strnlen. PF variant alias. Returns length of s limited to maxlen.
requirements: s must point to a readable region up to maxlen bytes or a shorter NUL-terminated string.

functions.name: memcpy_PF
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to memcpy. PF variant alias. Copies n bytes from src to dest. Returns dest.
requirements: dest must be writable for at least n bytes.
src must be readable for at least n bytes.
Memory regions must not overlap; use memmove if they do.

functions.name: strcpy_PF
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to strcpy. PF variant alias. Copies src to dest including NUL. Returns dest.
requirements: dest must be writable with capacity >= strlen(src)+1.
src must be a valid NUL-terminated string.
No overlapping buffers.

functions.name: strncpy_PF
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to strncpy. PF variant alias. Copies up to n bytes; pads with NUL or may leave dest unterminated. Returns dest.
requirements: dest must be writable for at least n bytes.
src must be readable.
Caller must ensure NUL-termination if needed when src length >= n.

functions.name: strcat_PF
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to strcat. PF variant alias. Appends src to dest. Returns dest.
requirements: dest must be a writable, NUL-terminated string with sufficient remaining space.
src must be a valid NUL-terminated string.
No overlapping buffers.

functions.name: strlcat_PF
functions.signature: size_t strlcat_PF(char *dest, const char *src, size_t size)
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to strlcat. PF variant alias. Appends with size-bound and returns length attempted.
requirements: dest must be NUL-terminated unless size is 0 and have a buffer of at least size bytes.
src must be NUL-terminated.
Check return value >= size for truncation.

functions.name: strncat_PF
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to strncat. PF variant alias. Appends up to n chars from src to dest and NUL-terminates. Returns dest.
requirements: dest must be a writable, NUL-terminated string with enough space for min(n, strlen(src)) + 1 bytes.
src must be NUL-terminated.
No overlapping buffers.

functions.name: strcmp_PF
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to strcmp. PF variant alias. Compares two strings; returns <0, 0, >0.
requirements: s1 and s2 must be valid NUL-terminated strings.

functions.name: strncmp_PF
functions.signature: int strncmp_PF(const char *s1, const char *s2, size_t n)
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to strncmp. PF variant alias. Compares up to n chars.
requirements: s1 and s2 must be readable strings.
n may be zero.

functions.name: strcasecmp_PF
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to strcasecmp. PF variant alias. Case-insensitive compare; returns <0, 0, >0.
requirements: s1 and s2 must be valid NUL-terminated strings.

functions.name: strncasecmp_PF
functions.signature: int strncasecmp_PF(const char *s1, const char *s2, size_t n)
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to strncasecmp. PF variant alias. Case-insensitive compare up to n.
requirements: s1 and s2 must be readable strings.
n may be zero.

functions.name: strstr_PF
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to strstr. PF variant alias. Substring search; returns pointer or NULL.
requirements: haystack and needle must be valid NUL-terminated strings.

functions.name: strlcpy_PF
functions.signature: size_t strlcpy_PF(char *dest, const char *src, size_t size)
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to strlcpy. PF variant alias. Bounded copy; returns length of src.
requirements: dest must be a writable buffer of at least size bytes (size may be zero).
src must be NUL-terminated.
Check return value >= size for truncation.

functions.name: memcmp_PF
functions.signature: int memcmp_PF(const void *s1, const void *s2, size_t n)
functions.description: Compatibility macro mapping to memcmp. PF variant alias. Compares n bytes; returns <0, 0, >0.
requirements: s1 and s2 must be readable memory regions of at least n bytes.
n may be zero.

functions.name: pgm_read_byte
functions.description: Compatibility macro that dereferences a byte at addr. On this platform it simply reads from RAM/flash via a regular pointer cast. Used to emulate AVR pgm_read_byte for PROGMEM access.
requirements: addr must be a valid pointer to at least 1 readable byte.
addr should be suitably aligned for byte access on the target (usually no alignment restriction for bytes).
Behavior is undefined if addr is invalid or points to unmapped memory.

functions.name: pgm_read_word
functions.description: Compatibility macro that reads a 16-bit value from addr via a direct dereference. Emulates AVR pgm_read_word for PROGMEM on non-AVR.
requirements: addr must be a valid pointer to at least 2 readable bytes.
addr must be correctly aligned for 16-bit access on the target architecture to avoid faults or undefined behavior.
Endianness is that of the target platform; no byte swapping is performed.

functions.name: pgm_read_dword
functions.description: Compatibility macro that reads a 32-bit value from addr via a direct dereference. Emulates AVR pgm_read_dword.
requirements: addr must be a valid pointer to at least 4 readable bytes.
addr must be correctly aligned for 32-bit access on the target architecture.
Endianness follows the target platform; no conversion is performed.

functions.name: pgm_read_float
functions.description: Compatibility macro that reads a float value from addr via direct dereference. Emulates AVR pgm_read_float.
requirements: addr must be a valid pointer to at least sizeof(float) readable bytes.
addr must be correctly aligned for float access on the target architecture.
Binary representation and endianness must match the platform’s float format.

functions.name: pgm_read_ptr
functions.description: Compatibility macro that reads a pointer value from addr via direct dereference. Emulates AVR pgm_read_ptr.
requirements: addr must be a valid pointer to at least sizeof(void*) readable bytes.
addr must be correctly aligned for pointer-sized access on the target architecture.
The stored pointer value must be valid for subsequent use if it will be dereferenced.

functions.name: pgm_read_byte_near
functions.description: Alias of pgm_read_byte. Historically for near (lower) address spaces on AVR; identical here.
requirements: Same as pgm_read_byte.

functions.name: pgm_read_word_near
functions.description: Alias of pgm_read_word. Historically for near address space; identical here.
requirements: Same as pgm_read_word.

functions.name: pgm_read_dword_near
functions.description: Alias of pgm_read_dword. Historically for near address space; identical here.
requirements: Same as pgm_read_dword.

functions.name: pgm_read_float_near
functions.description: Alias of pgm_read_float. Historically for near address space; identical here.
requirements: Same as pgm_read_float.

functions.name: pgm_read_ptr_near
functions.description: Alias of pgm_read_ptr. Historically for near address space; identical here.
requirements: Same as pgm_read_ptr.

functions.name: pgm_read_byte_far
functions.description: Alias of pgm_read_byte. Historically for far (upper) address spaces on AVR; identical here.
requirements: Same as pgm_read_byte.

functions.name: pgm_read_word_far
functions.description: Alias of pgm_read_word. Historically for far address space; identical here.
requirements: Same as pgm_read_word.

functions.name: pgm_read_dword_far
functions.description: Alias of pgm_read_dword. Historically for far address space; identical here.
requirements: Same as pgm_read_dword.

functions.name: pgm_read_float_far
functions.description: Alias of pgm_read_float. Historically for far address space; identical here.
requirements: Same as pgm_read_float.

functions.name: pgm_read_ptr_far
functions.description: Alias of pgm_read_ptr. Historically for far address space; identical here.
requirements: Same as pgm_read_ptr.

A standard C string: a contiguous sequence of bytes terminated by a NUL (0x00) byte. May contain any non-NUL bytes before the terminator. Suitable for functions that expect const char* C-strings such as strlen, strcpy, strcat, strcmp, and their variants.

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# We generate arbitrary binary data buffers intended for use with length-bounded
# memory functions (memcmp/memcpy/memmem/memchr/memrchr). The buffers should be
# valid readable memory regions and often interesting when they contain specific
# byte patterns, repetitions, boundaries, and common substrings.
#
# Strategy:
# - Compose the output as a single bytes object that fuzzer harness will slice
#   into FUZZ_PARAM_STR buffers. While we don't control how many FUZZ_PARAM_STR
#   calls are made, providing a buffer with varied segments increases the chance
#   that independent extractions yield interesting contents.
# - Include segments of:
#   - Repeated single bytes (0x00, 0xFF, 0x20, 0x7F, 'A', 'a', '\\n')
#   - Incrementing/decrementing sequences
#   - Random data chunks of varying sizes
#   - Known English words and mixed-case text to trigger str* cases if used
#   - Embedded needles within haystacks for memmem hits and misses
#   - Palindromic and mirrored regions for memrchr behavior differences
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.
# - Seeded randomness ensures reproducibility per seed while still varying.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

COMMON_BYTES = [
    0x00, 0xFF, 0x20, 0x7F, ord('A'), ord('a'), ord('\n'), ord('0'), ord(' '), ord('X')
]

WORDS = [
    b"needle", b"haystack", b"TEST", b"test", b"Arduino", b"avr", b"PROGMEM",
    b"memcpy", b"memcmp", b"memchr", b"memrchr", b"memmem",
]


def _rand_len(rng: random.Random, lo: int, hi: int) -> int:
    return rng.randint(lo, hi)


def _repeated(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    bval = rng.choice(COMMON_BYTES)
    ln = _rand_len(rng, 1, 512)
    return bytes([bval]) * ln


def _inc_seq(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    ln = _rand_len(rng, 1, 512)
    start = rng.randrange(256)
    return bytes(((start + i) & 0xFF for i in range(ln)))


def _dec_seq(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    ln = _rand_len(rng, 1, 512)
    start = rng.randrange(256)
    return bytes(((start - i) & 0xFF for i in range(ln)))


def _random_chunk(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    ln = _rand_len(rng, 1, 1024)
    return rng.randbytes(ln)


def _text_chunk(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Build a chunk with words, mixed case, and separators including NULs.
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    count = _rand_len(rng, 3, 10)
    seps = [b" ", b",", b";", b"\n", b"\t", b"\x00"]
    for _ in range(count):
        w = rng.choice(WORDS)
        # Randomly change case of ASCII letters
        mut = bytearray()
        for c in w:
            if 65 <= c <= 90 or 97 <= c <= 122:
                if rng.random() < 0.3:
                    c = c ^ 0x20  # flip case
            mut.append(c)
        parts.append(bytes(mut))
        parts.append(rng.choice(seps))
    return b"".join(parts)


def _embed_needle_in_haystack(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Construct H + needle + T where needle appears multiple times and at edges
    base = rng.randbytes(_rand_len(rng, 5, 40))
    needle_len = _rand_len(rng, 1, 16)
    needle = rng.randbytes(needle_len)
    # Ensure some simple needles as well
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        needle = rng.choice(WORDS)
    prefix = rng.randbytes(_rand_len(rng, 0, 64))
    suffix = rng.randbytes(_rand_len(rng, 0, 64))
    middle_fill = rng.randbytes(_rand_len(rng, 0, 64))
    chunk = prefix + needle + middle_fill + needle + base + needle + suffix
    # Also place single-byte needle variations near boundaries
    if len(needle) > 0:
        nb = needle[:1]
        chunk = nb + chunk + nb
    return chunk


def _mirror_chunk(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    half = rng.randbytes(_rand_len(rng, 8, 128))
    return half + half[::-1]


def _boundary_mix(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Mix of small sizes including zeros for n==0 paths
    parts = [b"", b"\x00", b"\x00\x00", b"A", b"\xFF", b"B\x00C"]
    # Add small randoms
    for _ in range(_rand_len(rng, 1, 5)):
        parts.append(rng.randbytes(_rand_len(rng, 1, 8)))
    return b"".join(parts)


def _assemble(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    segments: List[bytes] = []
    builders = [
        _repeated, _inc_seq, _dec_seq, _random_chunk,
        _text_chunk, _embed_needle_in_haystack, _mirror_chunk, _boundary_mix,
    ]
    # Always include at least one of each principal pattern to maximize coverage
    for fn in builders:
        segments.append(fn(rng))
    # Add some extra random selections
    extra = _rand_len(rng, 3, 10)
    for _ in range(extra):
        segments.append(rng.choice(builders)(rng))
    data = b"".join(segments)
    if len(data) > MAX_TOTAL:
        data = data[:MAX_TOTAL]
    return data


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    buf = _assemble(rng)
    # Ensure non-empty sometimes; but allow empty with small probability
    if len(buf) == 0 or (rng.random() < 0.05 and len(buf) > 0):
        # 5% chance to return empty buffer to drive n==0 paths when harness bounds n by size
        return b""
    return buf

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces valid NUL-terminated C strings packed into a single
# byte buffer. The fuzzing harness will consume FUZZ_PARAM_STR values from the
# buffer in sequence. We therefore encode multiple C-strings back-to-back,
# each terminated with a single NUL (\x00). No filenames are required by the
# provided stubs.
#
# Design goals:
# - Provide a variety of string shapes to exercise different code paths:
#   empty strings, short ASCII, mixed case, numeric/hex-like, delimiter-rich,
#   repeated characters, long strings, unicode-UTF8 bytes (still valid as
#   opaque bytes before NUL), and strings with embedded spaces and punctuation.
# - Ensure every string is a valid C-string: never embed NUL except the final
#   terminator per string, so strlen/str* functions operate correctly.
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.
# - Deterministic under provided seed while allowing randomness to explore
#   many combinations.

ASCII_SAFE = (
    string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " "
).replace("\x00", "")

# A pool of delimiter-heavy character sets for functions like strsep/strpbrk/strspn
DELIM_SETS = [
    ",;:\t ",
    "|&:/\\\t\n ",
    "-=+*/%", 
    "()[]{}<>",
    "._-",
]

# Common substrings for strstr/strcasestr scenarios
COMMON_WORDS = [
    "hello", "world", "HELLO", "World", "Test", "test", "abc", "ABC",
    "Arduino", "progmem", "PROGMEM", "case", "Case", "cases", "needle",
    "haystack", "number", "12345", "deadBEEF", "beef", "BEEF", "fuzz",
]


def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return "".join(rng.choices(ASCII_SAFE, k=n))


def _rand_repeated(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    ch = rng.choice(ASCII_SAFE)
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ch * n


def _rand_delimited(rng: random.Random, min_tokens: int, max_tokens: int) -> str:
    # Build a string with tokens separated by randomly chosen delimiters
    tokens = []
    tcount = rng.randint(min_tokens, max_tokens)
    for _ in range(tcount):
        # Mix letters/digits to aid comparisons/case-insensitive ops
        tok = _rand_ascii(rng, 0, 8)
        tokens.append(tok)
    delim_set = rng.choice(DELIM_SETS)
    # Create a delimiter string of random length using the chosen set
    delims = "".join(rng.choices(delim_set, k=rng.randint(1, 3)))
    return delims.join(tokens)


def _rand_case_mix(rng: random.Random, base: str) -> str:
    out = []
    for ch in base:
        if ch.isalpha() and rng.random() < 0.5:
            out.append(ch.swapcase())
        else:
            out.append(ch)
    return "".join(out)


def _ensure_contains(hay: str, needle: str, rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Insert needle into hay at random position
    pos = rng.randint(0, len(hay))
    return hay[:pos] + needle + hay[pos:]


def _build_string_set(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    strings: List[str] = []

    # 1) Empty string
    strings.append("")

    # 2) Short ASCII
    strings.append(_rand_ascii(rng, 1, 12))

    # 3) Mixed case words with spaces
    base = rng.choice(COMMON_WORDS) + " " + rng.choice(COMMON_WORDS)
    strings.append(_rand_case_mix(rng, base))

    # 4) Numeric and hex-like
    hexpart = "deadbeef" if rng.random() < 0.5 else "DEADBEEF"
    strings.append("0x" + hexpart + str(rng.randint(0, 9999)))

    # 5) Delimiter-rich for strsep/strpbrk/strspn
    strings.append(_rand_delimited(rng, 3, 8))

    # 6) Repeated char sequences (good for strrchr/strchr)
    strings.append(_rand_repeated(rng, 1, 32))

    # 7) Long-ish random ASCII (bounded to keep global size in check)
    strings.append(_rand_ascii(rng, 64, 256))

    # 8) Needle/haystack pairs crafted to sometimes match and sometimes not
    n1 = rng.choice(COMMON_WORDS)
    h1 = _rand_ascii(rng, 5, 30)
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        h1 = _ensure_contains(h1, _rand_case_mix(rng, n1 if rng.random() < 0.5 else n1.lower()), rng)
    strings.append(h1)
    strings.append(n1)

    # 9) Case-insensitive variants
    n2 = rng.choice(COMMON_WORDS)
    h2 = _rand_ascii(rng, 5, 30)
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        h2 = _ensure_contains(h2, _rand_case_mix(rng, n2), rng)
    strings.append(h2)
    strings.append(_rand_case_mix(rng, n2))

    # 10) Strings with punctuation clusters to test strchr/strrchr/strpbrk
    punct = ''.join(rng.choices(string.punctuation, k=rng.randint(3, 12)))
    strings.append(_ensure_contains(_rand_ascii(rng, 5, 25), punct, rng))

    # 11) Whitespace-focused input to exercise spacers and width handling in printf
    ws = ''.join(rng.choices([' ', '\t'], k=rng.randint(1, 8)))
    strings.append(ws + _rand_ascii(rng, 1, 16) + ws)

    # 12) Paths-like content for slash/backslash coverage
    path_parts = [ _rand_ascii(rng, 1, 6) for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 5)) ]
    sep = rng.choice(["/", "\\"])
    strings.append(sep + sep.join(path_parts))

    # 13) Alphanumeric token soup
    soup = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 8)):
        soup.append(_rand_ascii(rng, 1, 6))
    strings.append(" ".join(soup))

    # 14) Explicit small keywords often used in comparisons
    strings.append(rng.choice(["a", "A", "z", "Z", "0", "9"]))

    # 15) Ensure presence of very short and mid-size tokens for strn* functions
    strings.append(_rand_ascii(rng, 1, 4))
    strings.append(_rand_ascii(rng, 8, 24))

    # 16) Delimiter sets themselves as inputs (useful for strsep delimiters)
    strings.append(rng.choice(DELIM_SETS))

    # 17) Another delimiter set variant
    strings.append(rng.choice(DELIM_SETS))

    # 18) A token string with many different punctuation characters
    diverse = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(10, 30)):
        diverse.append(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits))
        if rng.random() < 0.2:
            diverse.append(rng.choice(string.punctuation))
    strings.append(''.join(diverse))

    # Cap each string length to avoid overly large buffers per string
    capped = []
    for s in strings:
        if len(s) > 512:
            capped.append(s[:512])
        else:
            capped.append(s)

    return capped


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    strings = _build_string_set(rng)

    # Randomly add a few more strings to increase diversity per seed
    extra = rng.randint(2, 6)
    for _ in range(extra):
        choice = rng.random()
        if choice < 0.2:
            strings.append("")
        elif choice < 0.4:
            strings.append(_rand_ascii(rng, 1, 40))
        elif choice < 0.6:
            strings.append(_rand_delimited(rng, 2, 6))
        elif choice < 0.8:
            strings.append(_rand_repeated(rng, 1, 40))
        else:
            # Insert a word into a haystack
            n = rng.choice(COMMON_WORDS)
            h = _ensure_contains(_rand_ascii(rng, 5, 20), _rand_case_mix(rng, n), rng)
            strings.append(h)

    # Assemble into a single byte buffer with NUL termination per string
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    total = 0
    budget = 4096
    for s in strings:
        b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')  # safe: functions treat as bytes until NUL
        if b"\x00" in b:
            # Remove any accidental NULs (shouldn't appear from utf-8/ASCII set)
            b = b.replace(b"\x00", b"")
        needed = len(b) + 1  # plus terminator
        if total + needed > budget:
            break
        parts.append(b)
        parts.append(b"\x00")
        total += needed

    return b"".join(parts)
